items.back: `main.js:23` returns `false` with no status. If a future caller awaits the result to close a dialog, it will stay open with no explanation.

items.front: 3: Clue completion uses an open-time baseline.
items.back: `main.js:30` / `:41` (drill 7b) — safe but forces a reopen after any change elsewhere, including an unrelated category rename.

items.label: f04-generic-errors
items.front: Senior-review finding 1: validation in store.js:20-21 throws 'Points must be...' or 'Prompt must contain...'. What is missing and how would you fix it?
items.back: The message does not identify the record, so repairing a 2 MiB import means hunting. The validator already has category and question indices in scope inside its map callbacks; include them (and the category name) in the thrown message.

items.front: 7: Whole-board CAS is coarse by design.
items.back: `store.js:53` compares the full serialized board, so any write anywhere conflicts with any open editor. Documented as a limit (chapter 02) — reviewers should expect that, not flag it as a bug, until per-record versions exist.

`main.js:32` writes `question.answer` into a hidden element; anyone with devtools can read it. Fine for a local study tool, but the README's "Reveal answer" should not be mistaken for secrecy (practice exercise 5).

`error()` (`main.js:10`) writes the same message to the page panel, the editor and the clue dialog. An editor validation error therefore also appears in the main error panel behind the modal, and the panel is only cleared by the next successful operation or `load()`.

items.label: f03-coarse-cas
items.front: store.js:53 compares the whole serialized board. Why should a reviewer not flag 'two tabs editing different questions conflict' as a bug?
items.back: Whole-board CAS is coarse by design and documented as a limit. Fixing it needs per-record versions (e.g. a server database with conditional updates), which is a later exercise - not a tweak to this comparison.

items.front: 1: Validation errors do not identify the record.
items.back: `store.js:5`, `:7`, `:20` throw generic messages ("Invalid question fields.", "Prompt must contain...", "Points must be...") with no category or question index. For imports this makes a 2 MiB file very hard to repair.

items.label: f01-one-winner
items.front: Which invariant must survive any framework change in front of BoardStore (test/store.test.js:106-119)?
items.back: Two cooperating savers sharing one baseline produce exactly one winner and one revision: Promise.allSettled shows 1 fulfilled and 1 rejected save, and the stored revision is 1.

items.label: f02-lock-vs-cas
items.front: In BoardStore.save (store.js:51-59), what does deleting line 53 break, and why would removing the lock on line 51 instead still leave a window?
items.back: Without line 53 (the baseline compare) tab B overwrites tab A. Without the lock, lines 52-59 still run uninterrupted within one tab (no await), but tabs may run in separate processes and localStorage has no atomic read-modify-write across them, so two compare-then-write sequences can interleave.

`removeCategory(state, id)` reuses `id` as the inner filter parameter (`store.js:64`: `.filter(id => retained.has(id))`). Behaviour is correct, but the outer `id` is unreachable inside that callback; renaming avoids a future bug.

items.prompt: The stored board is valid JSON of 1.5 million characters, but most of them are emoji that take 4 bytes each in UTF-8. What does parseState do?
